item.title: Retry transient HTTP failures with capped, jittered exponential backoff
item.summary: A request that fails for a temporary reason is sent again, with each wait twice as long as the last up to a ceiling, plus a little randomness so many clients do not retry at the same moment.
item.details:
- Only rate-limit and service-unavailable responses are retried; other failures return at once.
- The attempt limit (`MaxAttempts`) bounds the total delay.
- The wait respects cancellation.

cases.unit_text:
MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 50


def split_into_batches(documents, max_bytes):
    """Group documents so each batch stays under both the count and size limits."""
    batches, current, current_bytes = [], [], 0
    for doc in documents:
        size = len(doc.payload)
        if current and (len(current) == MAX_BATCH_SIZE or current_bytes + size > max_bytes):
            batches.append(current)
            current, current_bytes = [], 0
        current.append(doc)
        current_bytes += size
    if current:
        batches.append(current)
    return batches

item.title: Greedy packing of documents under a count and a size cap
item.summary: Documents are added in order to the open batch, and a new batch starts whenever the next document would break either limit, so no batch is too large or too long.
item.details:
- One pass, linear in the number of documents.
- A single document larger than the byte cap still forms its own batch rather than being dropped.

cases.unit_text:
4 Incremental Indexing
Our approach builds the index incrementally. Instead of rebuilding the full inverted index after every update, new documents are written to a small in-memory segment that is merged into the main index once it exceeds a size threshold. This keeps write latency low while bounding the number of segments a query must scan.
In our experiments the merge threshold of 64 MB gave the best balance between write throughput and query latency (see Table 2).

item.title: Buffer new documents in a small segment and merge later
item.summary: New writes land in a small memory segment that is folded into the main index only when it grows past a limit (e.g. 64 MB), which keeps writes fast without letting queries face too many segments.
item.details: The authors treat the size limit as the tuning point between write throughput and query latency.
